segments.t: As the episode opens, Nina is busy helping her children Slavik and Yulia prepare their stage costumes for the upcoming City Day celebration. They are supposed to perform a song from the beloved animated film The Bremen Town Musicians. Slavik grumbles about his role and complains that nothing feels right, while Nina tries to keep everyone motivated. Let's listen to their conversation in Russian first.
Только не волнуйся, всё будет хорошо.
Ты у меня настоящая красавица!
Спасибо, мама! Ну как, Славик?
Конечно, тебе хорошо, ты трубадур!
Попробуй сама надеть костюм осла.
Я предлагала тебе быть петухом.
А я вообще хотел быть котом!
И кто тогда будет громко кукарекать?
Почему я должен кричать со сцены?
Славик, ну ты вечно всем недоволен!
Тебе всегда ничего не нравится.
Скоро начнётся наш вечер самодеятельности.
Мы споём песню бременских музыкантов.
Now let's examine Nina, Slavik, and Yulia's conversation line by line.

'Just don't worry, everything will be fine.' Nina comforts her daughter.

'Thanks, Mom! Well how is it, Slavik?' Yulia turns to her brother to ask for his opinion.

'Of course it's good for you, you're the troubadour!' Slavik points out Yulia's glamorous role.

'Try putting on the donkey costume yourself.' This phrase challenges her to wear the ridiculous costume.

'I offered to let you be the rooster.' The past tense feminine verb recalls an earlier offer.

'And I actually wanted to be the cat!' The past masculine verb expresses his true preference.

'And who will loudly crow then?' The compound future question points out the missing role.
